answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with earned, time-locked transaction quotas: a fresh identity starts on an island of its own, able to do almost nothing, and only gains higher limits after weeks of attested useful work. Like a juniper that grows slowly, reputation cannot be bought in bulk, so each fake identity must burn weeks of real compute on real tasks before it can transact at scale. A nebula of ten thousand sock puppets therefore costs ten thousand identities' worth of sustained effort, while one honest agent simply keeps working. Attack cost becomes linear in time and work, not free.
